city.Nigeria.description: This big, busy country in West Africa is bursting with music and movies. It is home to a film industry nicknamed Nollywood, catchy Afrobeats music, and ancient Nok clay statues made long, long ago.
city.Nigeria.landmark: massive Zuma Rock monolith rising beside the plains near Abuja
city.Nigeria.greeting: In Hausa, one of Nigeria's many languages, hello is “Sannu” (SAH-noo).
city.Nigeria.flag: three tall stripes of green, white, and green
city.Nigeria.clue.0: booked a ticket toward a big, busy country in West Africa
city.Nigeria.clue.1: wanted to visit the movie capital nicknamed 'Nollywood' that films tons of new stories
city.Sao Tome and Principe.description: This tiny two-island country sits in the warm Gulf of Guinea off Central Africa. Its steep volcanic peaks are cloaked in thick rainforest full of rare birds and plants found nowhere else on Earth.
city.Sao Tome and Principe.landmark: sharp volcanic spire of Pico Cão Grande towering above the rainforest
city.Sao Tome and Principe.greeting: Most people speak Portuguese — say hello with “Olá” (oh-LAH).
city.Sao Tome and Principe.flag: pinned on a flag badge: green and yellow stripes with two little black stars and a red triangle at the side
city.Sao Tome and Principe.clue.0: planned a boat trip to a pair of tiny islands off the coast of Central Africa
city.Senegal.description: This West African country reaches out to the Atlantic at Africa's westernmost point. It is known for its warm welcome, lively drumming and dancing, and a strange lake that shimmers bright pink from salt-loving algae.
city.Senegal.landmark: bright pink water of Lac Rose with salt-collectors' pirogues
city.Senegal.greeting: In Wolof, a friendly hello is “Na nga def?” (nah-gah-DEF) — it means “How are you?”
city.Senegal.flag: green, yellow and red stripes with a single green star in the middle
city.Senegal.clue.0: couldn't wait to see a lake that glows bright pink from tiny salt-loving algae
city.Senegal.clue.1: kept talking about a giant bronze statue in the capital taller than the Statue of Liberty
city.Seychelles.description: This nation of islands is scattered across the Indian Ocean northeast of Madagascar. It is famous for powder-white beaches, lumbering giant tortoises, and a palm that grows the biggest, heaviest seed of any plant on Earth.
city.Seychelles.landmark: smooth pink granite boulders on the turquoise beach of Anse Source d'Argent

city.Sierra Leone.description: This West African country on the Atlantic coast takes its name, meaning "Lion Mountains," from the peaks above its capital, Freetown. It has green rainforests, chimpanzee sanctuaries, and some of the world's finest diamonds.
city.Sierra Leone.landmark: palm-lined white beach beneath the green Lion Mountains near Freetown
